name: Old Parliament Building

description:
The Old Parliament Building, completed in 1930, is a stunning Neo-Baroque structure that served as Sri Lanka's legislature for 53 years. Built on the idea of Sir Henry McCallum and designed by A. Woodson, it now houses the Presidential Secretariat and stands as a proud reminder of Sri Lanka's colonial past and journey to independence in 1947.

**🕒** Mon–Fri 8:30am–4:30pm

name: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque
shortDescription: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque combines Indo-Islamic, Persian, Gothic revival, and Neoclassical architecture. Famed for its striking red and white candy-striped brick facade, the Red Mosque is a long-standing landmark on Second Cross Street in Pettah.

name: Colombo City
shortDescription: Colombo is Sri Lanka's commercial capital blending colonial heritage, modern skyscrapers, beaches, shopping malls, and vibrant nightlife. Landmarks include the Lotus Tower, Galle Face Green, Pettah Market, and Beira Lake.

name: Gangaramaya Temple
shortDescription: Gangaramaya is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Colombo, started by Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Nayaka Thera in the late 19th century. Today it serves as a temple, cultural and educational center.

shortDescription: Galle Face Green is a popular ocean-side park known for sunset views, street food stalls, and leisure activities. Originally laid out in 1859 by Governor Sir Henry George Ward.

name: Yala National Park
shortDescription: Established in 1938, Yala National Park is famous for one of the highest concentrations of leopards in the world. Home to elephants, crocodiles, bears, deer, peacocks, and many migratory birds.
